children.text: **The Skeletal Dynamics Distal Elbow System consists of the following systems**
The Skeletal Dynamics Align Radial Head System features precision-engineered titanium alloy implants designed to restore radial head anatomy and optimize elbow stability
Included in the system are cobalt-chrome modular components, cannulated instrumentation, and specialized tools for precise radial head reconstruction
replacement of the radial head for degenerative or post-traumatic disabilities
with the elbow flexed 90 degrees, palpate and mark the lateral epicondyle

images.caption: With the elbow flexed 90 degrees, palpate and mark the lateral epicondyle. Make an 8 -10cm line through the marked point.

children.text: make an 8 -10cm line through the marked point
to identify the axis of forearm rotation, pronate the hand and flex the wrist
palpate and mark the ulnar styloid, ulnar head and the direction of the shaft

images.caption: Palpate and mark the ulnar styloid, ulnar head and the direction of the shaft.

children.text: note: use fluoroscopic imaging to verify proper landmark placement
make a longitudinal facial incision over the center of the capitellum for the Kaplan approach

images.caption: Make a longitudinal fascial incision over the center of the capitellum for the Kaplan approach

children.text: open the join and gain access to the radial head

images.caption: Open the joint and gain access to the radial head.

children.text: limit distal dissection to protect the radial nerve
assemble and measure them using the Radial Head Sizing Tray

images.caption: Remove the radial head fragments; assemble and measure them using the Radial Head Sizing Tray.

children.text: note: if between radial head sizes, select the smaller

images.caption: Radial Head Sizing Tray

children.text: select the Trial Head that corresponds to the native head

images.caption: Select the Trial Head that corresponds to the native head.
Trial Heads

children.text: with the forearm pronated, select the radial neck length using the Neck Sizing Gauges

images.caption: With the forearm pronated, select the radial neck length using the Neck Sizing Gauges.

children.text: note: if between two lengths, always select the shortest sizing option
use the Neck Sizing Gauge to select the level of the desired radial cut

images.caption: Use the Neck Sizing Gauge to select the level of the desired radial cut. Mark the radial neck just distal to the Neck Sizing Gauge.

children.text: mark the radial neck just distal to the Neck Sizing Gauge
secure the Bone Holding Forceps just distal to the marked radial neck

images.caption: Secure the Bone Holding Forceps just distal to the marked radial neck.

children.text: lift the radius with the Bone Holding Forceps, then make the radial neck cut

images.caption: Lift the radius with the Bone Holding Forceps, then make the radial neck cut.

children.text: note: the maximum defect that can be corrected is 23mm
starting with the smallest Rasp, position the hand in pronation and insert the Rasp past the tuberosity in the direction of the radial styloid

images.caption: Starting with the smallest Rasp, position the hand in pronation and insert the Rasp past the tuberosity in the direction of the radial styloid

children.text: note: this will establish the trajectory for all subsequent Rasps
fully insert each of the rasps up to the proximal depth mark using an oscillating motion

images.caption: Fully insert each of the rasps up to the proximal depth mark using an oscillating motion.

children.text: continue sequential rasping until cortical bone is encountered
note the size of the final rasp used
while final rasp is still fully inserted, maintain positive pressure and perform counter clockwise rotation prior to removing
note: do not use rasps under power
if the radial cut is not coplanar with the proximal depth mark of the rasp, planing may be required for proper seating of the prosthesis

images.caption: If the radial cut is not coplanar with the proximal depth mark of the rasp, planing may be required for proper seating of the prosthesis.

children.text: with the final rasp fully seated, mark the highest point on the radius to identify the area to be planed
prepare the respected end of the radius using the planer

images.caption: Prepare the resected end of the radius using the Planer.
Planer

children.text: with the forearm pronated, confirm the final radial neck length using the Neck Sizing Gauges

images.caption: With the forearm pronated, confirm the final radial neck length using the Neck Sizing Gauges.

children.text: note: if between two lengths, always select the shortest sizing option.
select the Trial Stem that corresponds to the final Rasp/Planer used and insert it into the prepared canal

images.caption: Select the Trial Stem that corresponds to the final Rasp/ Planer used and insert it into the prepared canal.

children.text: assemble the Trial Head and Neck by threading the two components together

images.caption: Assemble the Trial Head and Neck by threading the two components together.

children.text: thread the handle of the Neck Sizing Gauge into the Trial Head to facilitate loading onto the Trial Stem
assemble the Trial Head and Neck into the Trial Stem
reduce the joint and assess the sizing of the trial components by manipulating the elbow through its full range of motion

images.caption: Reduce the joint and assess the sizing of the trial components by manipulating the elbow through its full range of motion.

children.text: note: ensure that the joint has not been over-stuffed
confirm a proper fit using fluoroscopy, then remove the trial components

images.caption: Confirm a proper fit using fluoroscopy, then remove the trial components.

children.text: in a true A/P view of the proximal forearm in supination, confirm that the height of the radial head trial is at or distal to the corner formed by the lesser and greater sigmoid notches
also, confirm proper radial head diameter by assuring that the apex of the capitellum is centered over the radial head
with the forearm in pronation, use the Bone Holding Forceps to lift the radius out of the wound, then insert the Radial Stem implant into the canal

images.caption: With the forearm in pronation, use the Bone Holding Forceps to lift the radius out of the wound, then insert the Radial Stem implant into the canal.

children.text: if the Radial Stem cannot be inserted by hand to a depth covering more than half of the TPS coated area, remove the stem and see optional next step

images.caption: If the Radial Stem cannot be inserted by hand to a depth covering more than half of the TPS coated area, remove the stem and see optional step 20 on the following page.

children.text: use the next larger sized Rasp and insert it up to the distal depth mark (A) to slightly enlarge the proximal portion of the intramedullary canal in a counter clockwise motion

images.caption: Use the next larger sized Rasp and insert it up to the distal depth mark (A) to slightly enlarge the proximal portion of the intramedullary canal in a counter clockwise motion.

children.text: reinsert the stem to confirm adequate insertion depth (at least half of the TPS coated section)
insert the Stem Impactor laterally, then lower the handle until in-line with the stem

images.caption: Insert the Stem Impactor laterally, then lower the handle until in-line with the stem.
Impactor

children.text: impact the stem until the collar seats flush against the radius
note: the notch on the Stem Impactor facilitates loading
side load the Radial Head implant onto the stem, then rotate it until the threads are positioned laterally

images.caption: Side load the Radial Head implant onto the stem, then rotate it until the threads are positioned laterally.

children.text: note: each Radial Head implant is packaged with its respective Lock Screw
remove the Bone Holding Forceps and secure the Head Alignment Tool to the Radial Head
the two tines of the Head Alignment Tool should engage the grooves of the Radial Head

images.caption: Head Alignment Tool engagement grooves
The two tines of the Head Alignment Tool should engage the grooves of the Radial Head.

children.text: note: the Head Alignment Tool is used to control the position of the Radial Head
loosely thread the Lock Screw into the Radial Head

images.caption: Loosely thread the Lock Screw into the Radial Head.

children.text: keeping the Head Alignment Tool connected to the Radial Head, slide the rail of the Forearm Axis Jig into the handle until it snaps securely

images.caption: Keeping the Head Alignment Tool connected to the Radial Head, slide the rail of the Forearm Axis Jig into the handle until it snaps securely.

children.text: with the elbow flexed and the forearm in neutral, adjust and lock the distal end of the Forearm Axis Jig to the marked fovea of the ulna
pronate the Head Alignment Tool ~20 - 30 degrees from the neutral forearm position, then tighten the Lock Screw while providing counter-torque

images.caption: Pronate the Head Alignment Tool ~20 - 30 degrees from the neutral forearm position, then tighten the Lock Screw while providing counter-torque.

children.text: warning: the Head Alignment Tool must be used when tightening the Lock Screw to provide the necessary counter-torque
note: positioning the Head Alignment Tool in 20 - 30 degrees of pronation ensures the Lock Screw is at the center of the “safe zone”
use the torque indicating T-Handle Driver to ensure the minimal torque has been achieved

images.caption: Use the torque indicating T-Handle Driver to ensure the minimal torque has been achieved.

children.text: if desired, additional torque can be gained using the Universal Driver Handle
warning: the Head Alignment Tool must be used when tightening the Lock Screw to provide the necessary counter-torque
remove the Forearm Axis Guide assembly
manipulate the elbow through its full range of motion to confirm final implant alignment

images.caption: Manipulate the elbow through its full range of motion to confirm final implant alignment.

children.text: confirm final implant alignment using fluoroscopic imaging

images.caption: Confirm final implant alignment using fluoroscopic imaging.

children.text: repair soft tissues as needed, then close the incision

images.caption: Repair soft tissues as needed, then close the incision.
